summary.headline: Goodluck India Q1 FY27 standalone revenue up ~23% to INR1,205.9 cr, EBITDA up 15% to INR110.5 cr; Defence expansion delayed 6-9 months.
summary.overview: Standalone income from operations rose to INR1,205.94 crore from INR983.29 crore YoY, while standalone EBITDA rose 15% to INR110.53 crore and PAT rose to INR49.66 crore from INR40.14 crore. Management cited 31% consolidated revenue growth, 46% consolidated EBITDA growth and 67% consolidated PAT growth, with EBITDA margin above 10%. Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace) won orders of INR255 crore and INR52 crore for 155 mm shells, but its capacity expansion has slipped 6-9 months due to financial closure. A preferential issue at the Defence subsidiary (about 75 lakh shares at INR375, about INR285 crore) drew heavy shareholder criticism over valuation and the choice over a rights issue at parent level.

vs INR40.14 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA margin

segments.name: Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA margin. Orders of INR255 crore (about 50,000 shells of 155 mm long-range RTF empty shells, 10-month execution) and INR52 crore (20,000 shells, 3-month execution). DGQA certificate received for 107 RTF artillery shells.

segments.name: Precision tubes / auto tubes
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 12-13%. Hydraulic tube utilisation rose to 60-65% in Q1 from about 50%.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 10-11%. Transmission tower capacity about 50,000 tons per year.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance maintained at 15-20% for FY27 (versus 14-15% in the prior call, per an analyst).
Defence FY27 revenue target INR300-350 crore at 30-35% EBITDA margin; management reiterated 30-35% margin range, saying it is conservative.
Defence expansion (250,000 shells capacity) delayed 6-9 months; management hopes expansion starts by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation about one year later (around Q4 FY28).
Post-expansion Defence plant capacity 400,000 shells, achievable about 350,000 shells per annum.
Earlier Defence FY28 target of INR1,000 crore (INR800 crore shells, INR200 crore aerospace) to move out by 6-9 months; management declined to give a new FY28 number.
Capex: Defence about INR400 crore; standalone INR100-150 crore.
Debt repayment for FY27 stated as INR62 crore (INR25 crore repaid in Q1), per CFO; analyst had noted a lower figure earlier.
Management said Defence subsidiary IPO could be in about 18 months, subject to approvals.

Value-added products about 60% of business; GI tube and front fork tube capacity expected in about 6 months; 40,000-45,000 metric tons of capacity addition announced for FY27 (large-diameter pipe ramp delayed by West Asia crisis).
capex_capacity: Defence shell capacity currently 150,000 shells per annum; expansion (plant capacity 400,000) delayed 6-9 months due to financial closure.
Defence capex about INR400 crore; standalone capex INR100-150 crore.
Hydraulic tube capacity utilisation 60-65% in Q1 (about 50% earlier).
Plans for aerospace rolling mill to supply outer bodies for space rockets and an aerospace supplier ecosystem; Goodluck Astra land allotted, licence applied for.
Large-diameter pipe and precision tube capacity additions (40,000-45,000 MT) ramping slower due to West Asia crisis.
demand_pricing: Overall realisation about INR7,000/ton in Q4; target INR9,000/ton within 3 years; management said it has not increased much in Q1 due to West Asia crisis.
Defence realisation roughly doubled between the 107 (18 km range) and ERFB (38 km range) shell orders; EBITDA per ton about INR9,000 in Q1.
Exports to more than 100 countries; growth coming from US and Europe; export order pipeline described as healthy; first-quarter export growth about 53% per management.
Solar: 30%+ market share. Transmission demand supported by solar evacuation from Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Input cost risk high due to petroleum-linked inputs and logistics costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Defence subsidiary being listed separately rather than demerged, and how does that create value for current shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers recommended a separate listing; the listing will be based on future numbers. Parent shareholders benefit as a subsidiary's value accrues to the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the subsidiary stake sold through a preferential issue instead of a rights issue at Goodluck India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers preferred this route and that the company needs funds for growth. Management acknowledged a differing view and said it would consider feedback.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary's implied valuation from the INR285 crore issue at INR375/share?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-issue outstanding shares about 4.91 crore; post-issue about 5.66 crore shares (about 75 lakh new shares). Implied valuation not explicitly stated; dilution cited as about 10.5% (an investor said 15%).

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Defence expansion slipped and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay is due to financial closure of the project and approvals; expansion now expected to start by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation around a year later.

qa_highlights.question: What are Defence margins and revenue in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Defence revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA; management is guiding 30-35% sustainable margin, stating it is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company maintaining its FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 15-20% revenue growth guidance; volume up 9% in Q1 and expected to improve if geopolitical conditions ease.

risks_watch: Defence capacity expansion (150,000 to 400,000 plant capacity) slipped 6-9 months on financial closure and approvals; management targets start by Q4 FY27 and commercialisation about a year later.

Defence subsidiary preferential issue (about 75 lakh shares at INR375, about INR285 crore) and the choice over a parent rights issue; management cited about 10.5% dilution, an investor cited 15%, and the valuation was not explicitly disclosed.
Input cost and logistics exposure from West Asia crisis and petroleum-linked inputs; management said realisation has not risen much (target INR9,000/ton within 3 years vs about INR7,000 in Q4).
Large-diameter pipe and precision tube capacity ramp (40,000-45,000 MT) slower due to West Asia crisis; GI and front fork tube capacity expected in about 6 months.
Debt repayment for FY27 now stated as INR62 crore (INR25 crore repaid in Q1), higher than the figure analysts had noted earlier.
Defence margin sustainability: management kept 30-35% guidance despite 38% in Q1 and about 42% in the prior quarter; Defence IPO targeted in about 18 months, subject to approvals.
key_quotes: We maintain our guidance that it should be 15% to 20%. As far as the volume this quarter, it has gone up by 9%.
We will definitely get it. It all depends on the approvals and regulatory systems because that is a major point in this all, whatever we plan, approvals and regulations are always important.
Management is also always conservative, and we like to be conservative. So we will remain -- we will keep this at 30% to 35%.
We have -- as far as this Defence is concerned, we have a lot of inquiries enough for the next 5 years. However, as a policy, we do not announce till we have technically and commercially clear order.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and demand, with volume up 9% and consolidated growth guidance of 15-20% maintained, but noticeably cautious and evasive on the subsidiary's fundraising structure, valuation and FY28 Defence targets, repeatedly deferring to approvals, advisers and future updates. Management repeatedly said it would "keep in mind" shareholder feedback on the preferential issue without giving a rationale on the rights-issue route.
